prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Make a detailed, inviting hand-painted molecular cartoon answering "T-DM1: where does cargo go?". This is one PRODUCT-SPECIFIC noncleavable antibody-drug-conjugate route, not every ADC. Target native1024x1536 portrait, clean calm contours, large recognizable molecules and physical nested compartments. Essential labels44–48px at1024 native width for326/358CSSpx reading. Short direct labels rather than text cards. No people, smiling cells, logos, copied source figures or clinical success/death scenes.

Top one-third: a spacious physical parts close-up. A recognizable slate-blue Y-shaped antibody has ONE conjugated attachment enlarged at its stem-side surface: short grey noncleavable linker connects a small coral DM1 payload symbol to the antibody. Direct labels "Antibody", "Noncleavable linker", "DM1" and small large-font note "One attachment enlarged". This is not a measured DAR depiction; no number/count of whole-product loading is shown. No linker-cutting scissors. The link physically touches both protein and payload.

Main scene: one complete target-cell cutaway with a CLOSED outer plasma-membrane contour, clearly separating "Outside" from "Cytosol" inside. The antibody binds a clearly transmembrane surface receptor labelled "HER2" at the upper-left cell edge. Its antigen-binding arm contacts HER2 outside; cargo stays attached. A short arrow "Uptake" leads into an ENCLOSED small uptake vesicle entirely inside the cell, containing the same bound/conjugated ADC. The vesicle is not a free antibody floating across a membrane. A second short route arrow leads to one large CLOSED membrane-enclosed lysosome inside the cell at center-left. Do not open the lysosome to the outside of the cell. Do not draw an intact antibody entering the cytosol, nucleus or tubulin.

Inside the lysosome, draw antibody fragments and one enlarged resulting active catabolite: a small amino-acid remnant, grey linker and coral DM1 symbol remain connected in that order. The antibody has been broken down; the NONCLEAVABLE linker is not cut. Direct labels "Antibody breakdown" and "Linker retained" identify these relationships. The catabolite is labelled "Active catabolite". No free DM1 alone is shown as the noncleavable processing product. Distinguish the enclosed lysosomal lumen from surrounding cytosol using large direct label "Lysosome lumen" and a short leader "Lysosomal membrane" to the continuous bilayer.

A sage schematic membrane transporter, labelled "SLC46A3", is inserted in the LYSOSOMAL membrane on its right side, NOT the cell surface. A single clear arrow takes the CONNECTED catabolite through this transporter from lumen INTO surrounding cytosol. Show the same amino-acid/linker/DM1 remnant outside after transport. There are no holes or spontaneous leak arrows elsewhere through this membrane. This is a simplified experimental route, not exact transporter helices/stoichiometry or an in-patient measurement.

In the cytosol to the lower-right, show recognizable microtubule tubes and tubulin building blocks, labelled "Tubulin" and "Microtubules". One transported connected catabolite contacts a tubulin building block at this action region; a short arrow "Action site" ends here. The active chemical remnant reaches susceptible machinery; the intact antibody never contacts this action site. Do not draw a nucleus, DNA, universal cell killing, tissue targeting, distant lesions or neighboring cells in this first cartoon. Outcome is not guaranteed. Keep the microtubule region INSIDE the same outer-cell boundary and OUTSIDE the lysosome. Do not let the outer cell boundary pass through any intracellular region.

Exact allowed text: "T-DM1: where does cargo go?", "Antibody", "Noncleavable linker", "DM1", "One attachment enlarged", "Outside", "Cytosol", "HER2", "Uptake", "Lysosome lumen", "Lysosomal membrane", "Antibody breakdown", "Linker retained", "Active catabolite", "SLC46A3", "Tubulin", "Microtubules", "Action site". No other prose. Use readable leaders with definite endpoints and sparse directional arrows. Molecular shapes, scales, attachment position and transporter shape are schematic, not an exact chemical structure or measured composition. No universal ADC biomarker, completion of delivery, clinical benefit or efficacy ranking. Do not copy a published figure.

Light palette: warm ivory paper and quiet navy ink; soft slate-blue protein contours, muted rose/sage cells, sand lysosome interior, subdued grey linker, coral DM1 symbols, dusty-violet DXd diamonds, gold FICTIONAL loading dots. Maintain matte hand-painted texture and calm outlines. No neon/glow/glossy3D rendering; color is a drawing convention, not a biological amount or efficacy code.
